A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same equilibrium sequence modeling work. Their complete main texts and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison of equations, tables, figures, and prose despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v5 reports original VirtualHome-Env planning experiments, computational-efficiency measurements, ablations, and convergence results in the main text and Appendix C.

after.justification: v6 retains these original results and adds ALFRED transfer evaluation, noisy-feedback experiments, and convergence measurements for two Qwen models.

M1.justification: The fixed-point formulation, supervised training objective, nested inference loops, equilibrium reuse, experience memory, and world model are unchanged. The new problem statement and expanded Figure 3 caption explain the existing procedure.

E1.justification: ALFRED changes from a discussed alternative in v5 to an evaluated zero-shot transfer benchmark in v6, without environmental feedback (Table 7). Table 5 also introduces corrupted-feedback scenarios in VirtualHome-Env. This extends coverage beyond the original benchmark and its ordinary feedback conditions.

E2.justification: The convergence comparison expands from original Llama, supervised-finetuned Llama, and Ours in v5 Table 5 to include original Qwen-2.5-0.5B and Qwen-2.5-7B in v6 Table 4. Existing planning comparator sets are retained; ALFRED uses the existing supervised Llama comparator.

E3.justification: New protocols include environmental-feedback-only evaluation with 0%, 5%, 10%, and 20% feedback corruption, and ALFRED testing without retraining using updated prompts, seven-category task classification accuracy, and action-object recall. Original VirtualHome splits, training budgets, metrics, and correction limits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v6 adds a feedback-corruption study testing sensitivity to incorrect feedback types, objects, or actions. It also extends the existing convergence analysis to Qwen models. The feedback-component ablations, efficiency analyses, and qualitative refinement traces are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions describe convergence measurements over 10 initial plans for each of 60 random tasks and report mean, standard deviation, minimum, and maximum. Figure 6 already reports mean and standard deviation. Additional Qwen rows retain this practice; the new noise and ALFRED tables introduce no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v6 adds distinct transfer and noise-response findings. ALFRED results are 54% versus 11% task classification accuracy and 27.08% versus 0.50% action-object recall for Ours versus SFT Llama. It also adds corrupted-feedback SR/GCR results and Qwen convergence means of 4.80 and 7.68 iterations. Matched existing planning and Llama convergence values are unchanged.

T1.justification: New Section 3.1 explicitly formulates the task using instructions, action sequences, and unobserved goal conditions, assuming a fully observed environment with coarse feedback. The equilibrium equations, gradient derivation, and implicit-function theorem proof remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about supervised self-refinement, efficient feedback incorporation, and inference-computation scaling. The added experiments do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v6 interprets the new experiments as showing tolerance to small amounts of feedback noise and better transfer without retraining. Appendix D additionally suggests vision-language models for addressing the retained visual-input limitation. Existing mechanism explanations and other limitations remain.

D1.justification: v6 briefly specifies how corrupted feedback is constructed and states that ALFRED evaluation uses updated prompts. The adapted prompts themselves are not supplied. Appendix B.3's training, sampling, inference, and timing details, along with code-access information, are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds robotic-planning citations to Silver, Zhang, Nayak, and Wang. Appendix D adds Yang et al. (2024b) and Athalye et al. for vision-language extensions. These broaden contextual references without substantially changing the work's positioning.

P1.justification: v6 adds a problem-statement subsection, renumbers the remaining method subsections, moves convergence discussion from Appendix C into Section 4.4, and adds short experimental passages and funding acknowledgements. Most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v6 adds the noise and ALFRED tables, relocates and expands the convergence table, and lengthens Figure 3's caption. Retained tables are renumbered and surrounding text reflows. Existing figure artwork and plot displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Compared with v5, v6 provides useful evidence on feedback corruption, transfer to ALFRED, and convergence beyond Llama, while making task assumptions more explicit. The improvement is limited: ALFRED evaluation uses proxy metrics without specifying its split, sample count, or adapted prompts, and the new noise and transfer results lack uncertainty estimates. These additions strengthen empirical support without changing the core method or original findings.
